When and why did you start training for fighting? A friend introduced me to it. At first, it was just something to do over the summer. I quickly realized that this is what I wanted to do.

What ranks and titles have you held? 2012 NJCAA Heavyweight National Champion, BJJ Brown Belt

Who is your favorite fighter, and why? My favorite fighter on the roster right now is Israel Adesanya because of his showmanship and high level striking

Do you have any heroes? My heroes outside of would be my father, not many men in my life have persevered thru more obstacles and grown stronger for those obstacles. He’s shown me what true sacrifice is and why it’s important to stay focused on whatever your goals are

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It's recognition for what I've done, but this is just the beginning; I want the belt.

What fight do you consider the key fight in your career? My fight vs JDS was the first fight I won without scoring a takedown and it showed me I can be dangerous on my feet

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? A cause close to my heart is spreading awareness about speech impediments, my father, daughter and myself all have one and I enjoy educating ppl on why having one means nothing outside of making someone speak a bit slower

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? What motivates me is my legacy at this point, I’d like to make the HOF and the best way to do that is to win fights in dominant fashion.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I didn't earn my degree, but I went to NIU and Harper College.

What was your job before you started fighting? Nightclub security

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? IKF National Champion

Favorite grappling technique: Single leg

Favorite Striking technique: Elbows

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: Outside of fighting I love spending time with my wife and daughter who’s 7. I enjoy traveling and creating memories with them. Some of my hobbies would include playing video games like Madden and Arc Raiders and reading. Ive always found solace in a good book and grew up reading sci-fi and fantasy novels going back to 2nd grade.

What’s one thing that you want UFC fans to know about you? One thing I’d like the world to know about me is a really chill humble guy, I don’t view myself as a celebrity or famous I’m just a dude who gets pad to beat up other dudes.

"I start with running. After that I work on my striking. Then I work on groundwork, jiu-jitsu. Then I'll spar with all of my partners. I'll get a fresh partner every couple of minutes and I just go until I can't moven any more."

UFC History

UFC 30

More Information

Curtis started training in boxing at age 15. "I used to want to be a boxer but when the UFC came out I knew that was what I wanted to do. I started watching tapes and training with anyone I could. I lived in Japan for a little while and trained with Enson Inoue and Carlos Newton, some of the Shooto guys over there. I was in the military so I was always gone but I always had training partners. Collegiate wrestlers. I just love training. I've always been athletic. I hooked up with the American Jiu-Jitsu guys and started training with them and that's where I am right now."

"I consider myself a natural striker. I am actually more trained in jiu-jitsu but it's a funny twist because I've never actually competed in boxing or kickboxing but it comes naturally to me. I do have serious training in jiu-jitsu though."

On making his UFC debut: "I feel great. It's a great opportunity. I'm sure it will be a great show."

Favorite grappling technique: Back take

Do you have any heroes? Not really....

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It’s a good way to beat the world’s best fighters.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I got my certification in France (same as college certification.)

What was your job before you started fighting? Police officer (special united group - CRS )

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Brown belt in BJJ (Checkmat / Bushido Academie), red belt in taekwondo

Favorite grappling technique: Kimura

When and why did you start training for fighting? I’ve always had a passion and interest in fighting. I’d be in the neighborhood with my gloves and asking about technique. I joined a formal gym when I was 17. I really looked to it for a way to get me and my family out of poverty.

What professional titles have you held? CFFC Champion 2x & Conflict Champion

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? Amateur Spartyka & Battle in the South Champion. I was 7-1 as an ammy with my only loss being against Tony Gravely in a rematch.

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? Black Belt in BJJ

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? The toughest fight to date would be with myself, the man in the mirror. If I can conquer him, I can conquer the world.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Myself. I am forever developing. I love my style and my ability to adapt to my opponents. My strategic mindset, athleticism, & my relentless pursuit of perfecting my craft and learning new skills.

What was your job before you started fighting? I’ve worked as a personal trainer – boxing class instructor, and when I lived in North Carolina I used to go on base and hold pads and help train.

Personal Life / Background: I like to go out in nature, the beach, the mountains, and I love to try new things. I have two brothers and I talk to them on a regular basis. I do not have any kids or pets. I have been traveling around a lot recently and seeing the world. I have been fighting my whole life. My grandfather was a boxer, so it came naturally to me. I was born to fight.

Other relevant information: I just started training at Tiger Muay Thai recently in Thailand. I still plan on training in Florida with my head coach Greg Choplin at KO Zone. While in Thailand, I have been training nonstop 2-3 times per day for the last 6 months until I got the call for the fight 2.5 weeks out.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I’ve been fighting my whole life. I love it. I grew up fighting, that was the environment I was raised in. So naturally when the chips fell how they may and life started lifing I found myself fighting. 

What does it mean for you to fight for the UFC? It means everything. All roads have led to this moment, this fight. I will show the UFC why they made the right decision signing me. I will put on a great performance en route to finishing Kai Kamaka on Saturday.

Who is your favorite fighter and why?  Josh Van is my favorite fighter because he’s a brother to me and always there training together and motivating each other. He’s a really selfless person and I do enjoy his fighting style as well. Amazing poise, shot selection, distance management and timing. 

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? Muhammad Ali 

What are your current ranks in martial arts? Purple Belt in BJJ

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? 11-1 Pro MMA and 12-1 as of Saturday after I win. 

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why? This win over Kai because it will show my skill level and put the entire division on notice after I beat a game opponent. 

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? There are many but one I hold closest is protecting endangered species around the globe.

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? There is only being the best in the planet. A defeater of men. Being the best is what sparks the fire that burns in me. Impossible for me to look beyond a championship.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Went to college but no degree. I went to the college of international ass whooping. I major in international cage fighting.  Seriously though I’ve traveled the world and been sponsored by international teams since 20 years old so that’s my education. I was educated by the world and how I navigated my experiences in it. 

What was your job before you started fighting? Many different jobs. Coaching and night club security are the main ones though. 

Favorite grappling technique: Anything that brings me victory.

Favorite Striking technique: Anything that brings me victory.

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: Fighting is my life. In between training I enjoy spending time in the forest away from all the noise of the city. Deep in nature as I should be.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started at 19 after moving to Aruba. I was trying to be something out of my family. I didn’t have much, but I had hunger. First it was boxing at Stay Thai Fit, then MMA, and I never looked back.

What professional titles have you held? None yet—but that changes soon. I came through the regional scene with finishes, and now I’m here to take over in the UFC.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? I went straight into pro fights after training, no amateur background—just boxing exhibitions to get experience. I believe real experience comes under lights with 4-ounce gloves.

Any belts/ranks in grappling disciplines? Blue belt in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu under Nova União. But belt or not—I’ll choke you if you give me your neck.

Any belts/ranks in striking disciplines? No formal belts, but I trained boxing and Muay Thai with real fighters. My hands speak louder than paper.

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? My toughest was the one I lost by DQ. I was dominating, but I let emotion take over. It taught me to stay calm, stay cold. That lesson made me a better fighter.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? José Aldo. He came from nothing, became a king, and never lost his heart. I train at his gym now—that shows you how things come full circle. Also- Israel Adesanya. I respect his creativity, striking IQ, and confidence. He performs at the highest level and keeps evolving. That’s the type of champion I’m working to become — but I’m building my own legacy.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? My heroes are my family. They believed in me from the beginning and sacrificed for me. They’re my foundation and my motivation.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? yes and i have my diploma of college —every day I’m learning how to survive, improve, and conquer.

What was your job before you started fighting? I’ve done construction, deliveries, cleaning. All that taught me how to grind.

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? I want to inspire young kids — especially those who come from small places — to believe in themselves. Discipline and hard work can change your life. I want to be proof of that.

Beyond a championship and money, what motivates you? I’m motivated by building a better life — not just for myself, but for my future kids and my future grandchildren. I want to create generational change. I’m coming for everything.

Origin of nickname: The Baba Yaga comes from a legend

Personal Life/Background (family stuff, kids, etc): I was born in Suriname, raised in Aruba from age 16. I come from a humble family—hard-working people. I carry them with me every time I step in the cage. No kids yet—right now my only focus is fighting.

Who are 3 people you'd love to meet or work with (celebrities, content creators, other fighters, sports stars)? Jose Aldo (which I did and now train with him), Israel Adesanya, Joe Rogan (would be sick to be on his podcast one day)

What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight? I love making content. I also like chilling with my team, playing FIFA, and just staying close to the people who keep me grounded.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I trained and competed in martial arts most of my life. However, with a stint in the military and deployments, that all stopped for at least a few years. I'd had an operation in 2008 and needed to get fit again, so kickboxing was it. I started in January 2009, I had a couple of amateur fights and was convinced to do BJJ, which led to my first amateur MMA fight, and from there I was addicted.

 
What ranks and titles have you held? I have the XFC Australia and Brace Australia lightweight title and recently successfully defended the XFC belt. I'm currently ranked third in Australia/New Zealand.

It's an opportunity to give back to those that have given so much to me. I'm married to the most patient person ever, as I'm sure most married fighters are, and this has always been my goal in the topic of fighting, so to give this opportunity back to her is rewarding in itself. Fighting in the UFC will give me opportunities I never thought existed.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started fighting after my sophomore year in college. I came home for the summer and did an MMA fight, which I won by TKO in 30 seconds and thought to myself, this is something I could be good at.

What ranks and titles have you held? Two-time Hawaii state MMA champion

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? Fighting for the UFC defines everything I've worked so hard for. 

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why? Theres so many good ones, wins and losses and I can’t define a single one. I’ve learned from every single fight and they’ve all made me better. I’ve competed with the best of the best and I know I’m right there.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? I have a few. Justin Gaethje just for the pure chaos and entertainment. Demetrius Johnson - world class mixed martial artist with high fight IQ. Max holloway - fellow Hawaiian brother I’ve learned a lot watching him.

Do you have any heroes? Jesus Christ. & I look up to my dad a lot. He's always displayed a noble character and defines the meaning of hard work. 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to Wartburg College in Waverly, Iowa and I studied kinesiology and nutrition.

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked construction, and I am currently working with a well-established MMA management company. 

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I've held 2 amateur titles in Hawaii.

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Black belt in BJJ, Brown Belt in Judo, NCAA D-III Wrestler

Favorite grappling technique: Kimura and taking the back

Favorite Striking technique: The Jab, because it sets up everything

Training: Boxing in the morning - Some footwork, some mitt work, some drilling and some sparring. At night - Wrestling and Jiu-Jitsu, Some nights Team Training - Sparring and preparing anyone with a fight coming up.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training when I was 13 years old. I started because I was always loved fighting when I was growing up. Every opportunity I got to fight someone, I took full advantage of it.

What ranks and titles have you held? 4x World Championship Fighting Champion, 2x Combat Zone Champion, 2x Rage In The Cage Champion, Full Force Champion, World Fighting League Champion, Wild Bill's Fight Night Champion.

Do you have any heroes? My Father is a hero of mine. He's an overachiever. He has a solution to everything. He doesn't start anything without finishing it.

What is your favorite technique? Triangle

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? Fighting in the UFC to me is a dream come true. Some kids growing up have dreams to play in the NFL, NBA, or MLB. But, not me - my dream has always been to fight in the UFC.

What was your job before you started fighting? I’ve always been a fighter

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Finished 6 fights by submission and 6 by knockout. Never been to a decision.

Favorite grappling technique: Triangle Choke

Favorite Striking technique: Left straight.
